mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rates compress equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate hiring freezes depress earnings growth.
failure_condition: The signal triggers in 10 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate broad consumer demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic growth fears accelerate.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (both HOUST and RSAFS declining) occurs in 15 instances but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production signals manufacturing output contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate profitability.
failure_condition: In the last 5 years, INDPRO decline periods (3 consecutive months) have produced positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly employment growth consistently signals robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through elevated earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate exceeding 0.2% indicates accelerating price pressures, prompting central bank tightening expectations that depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The signal triggers in 12 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent deceleration in quarterly GDP growth and monthly housing starts indicates weakening economic expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks mount.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (both GDPC1 and HOUST declining) occurs in 10 instances but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime characterized by rising federal funds rates, S&P 500 returns become negative over the next 60 trading days as higher discount rates reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: During the last 5 years, periods of rising FEDFUNDS (3 consecutive months of increase) have produced positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 45% of cases.
